Rosa, this is Gustavo from the travel desk. I have a problem and I do not think you can solve it, but I have to ask anyway. We booked twelve people on the Tuesday flight and the meeting moved to Thursday. The fare rules say we must pay a change fee on every ticket, which is more than the tickets cost us in the first place. I know I should have called you before we booked, and I did not. So my question is simple. Is there anything you can do, and if there is not, could you at least tell me what I should do differently next time? I would rather learn the rule than argue with it.

Two minutes on corporate policy, because this comes up on every call. There are three levels and people mix them up constantly. Level one, the rule. If the contract says the change fee applies, it applies, and none of us can remove it by being sympathetic. Level two, the guidelines. These are recommendations, not obligations, and you can depart from them if you can explain why. Level three, the exception. An exception must be requested, it must have a reason attached, and it must be approved by somebody above you. What you must never do is promise the exception before it is approved. If you do that, you have not helped the client. You have simply moved the bad news to somebody else's phone call.
